summary: The one Jan occurrence is already represented by gʕgs.II.t.preterit.1, with small transcription/punctuation differences and an XB 928 note. No duplicate example is added.

mgaʕgəsi is coordinated with šaʕiṯi after Mḥalqənne and may describe the clothes' state, rather than narrate a second finite event. Current evidence does not decide Preterit versus a depictive/result form.

The inherited entry has an unstructured Detransitive note but its structured stem is II and its box is Preterit with detransitive=false. This single repeated passage does not justify silently repairing that structure or changing the stem to Q.
The inherited translation's yellow and Jan machine translation's ragged differ. No fix-text or citation correction is proposed from machine English or presumed numbering offsets.
Check whether mgaʕgəsi in gʕgs.II.t.preterit.1 is finite Preterit or a state description, and whether the inherited Detransitive note should control its structured filing.
Identify the source concordance between the inherited XB 928 note and Jan 2.4/927 before adding a citation or changing the inherited number.
Check the meaning of šaʕiṯi and the inherited yellow translation against the actual source; Jan machine English cannot resolve it.
The tangled/piled clothes use repeats the inherited passage. It is not independent support for a new sense or an additional example.
